newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rossiya airline begins Moscow-Liepaja flights.
newsitem.headline: Rossiya airline begins Moscow-Liepaja flights.

text.p: Russia's state-owned Rossiya airline began scheduled passenger flights between Moscow and the Baltic sea port of Liepaja in Latvia on Friday, a company official said.
Mikhail Potemkin, deputy commercial director, told Reuters that the company operated 26-seat Yakovlev Yak-40 jet on the route on Mondays and Fridays.
"We hope these flights will be profitable due to big demand," he said.

Rossiya operates planes transporting the president and top government officials, but Potemkin said that the company also planned scheduled routes from Moscow to Omsk in Siberia and Krasnodar in the Southern Russia later this year.
"We also plan to begin scheduled flights to a few foreign destinations," he said not giving their names.
Currently, Rossyia operates about 20 aircraft, including a few jets to carry President Boris Yeltsin.
